Subject: CirrusScale: marketplace supplier intake - PO & onboarding forms

Hi Elena / CirrusScale ops team,

Thanks for the interest in listing on the Redwood-supported cloud marketplaces. To keep the procurement path smooth across AWS, Azure, and GCP we need a few items to complete vendor setup and to determine whether billing will flow via the marketplace (provider billing) or via a Redwood-issued PO.

Please provide the following if you haven't already:
- Completed vendor onboarding form (attached).
- W-9 or local tax certificate for US entity.
- Legal entity name that should appear on invoices and on the marketplace listing.
- Bank wiring instructions for direct-settlement (if you prefer invoiced PO instead of marketplace billing).

Notes on marketplace specifics (high level):
- AWS Marketplace: we can do a Transactable (AWS-billed) listing or a Private Offer (Redwood as purchaser) depending on your comfort with AWS billing flows. For Private Offers we will need Seller ID and prefer to sign a PO template.
- Azure Marketplace: publishability depends on Publisher ID and MPN enrollment; billing can be via Microsoft or via our marketplace procurement relationship.
- GCP Marketplace: requires a billing project mapping and partner terms; GCP billing + billing account ID are necessary for provider-billed offers.

Attached is the standard vendor intake PDF. If you prefer, we can start with a Private Offer/PO while we finish marketplace listing (this avoids delays to go-live).

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill and return onboarding_form + W-9 (attached).
2) Confirm whether you prefer marketplace-billing or Redwood PO-based invoicing.
3) If PO: sign the DocuSign we will send and provide bank details.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm billing flow and timeline?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick operational clarifications from marketplace side: 

1) AWS: if CirrusScale is happy to be transactable (AWS-billed), listing is usually fastest — that routes billing through AWS and you do not need a Redwood PO. Time-to-live typically 2–4 weeks once the offer is packaged and seller information (Seller ID, offer SKU, pricing) is in place. If CirrusScale prefers a Private Offer (Redwood-generated PO), that can be done immediately but requires a signed PO template and Redwood finops to accept private offer terms.

2) Azure: publisher enrollment can take longer (MPN/Publisher ID + co-sell paperwork). If you expect to sell into enterprises via Azure, plan for 3–6 weeks for full pub flow.

3) GCP: requires partner listing + billing project mapping. GCP often needs a mapped billing account and a partner-facing contract.

Please see attached marketplace_po_guidance.pdf for our PO template notes and typical fields we need mapped to your invoices (invoice remittance address, tax ID, and the PO number placement).

Elena — based on your preference for provider-billing, we can prioritize preparing the transactable AWS offer. Two asks for that path:
- Please confirm the legal entity name exactly as it should appear on the AWS Seller profile.
- Share any lead times for publishing (marketing content, logos, and compliance artifacts).

If you still want Redwood to issue an initial PO for a pilot, please let us know and we’ll route the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: marketplace_po_guidance.pdf
